subject: physics
title: First equation of motion
explanation: Under constant acceleration the velocity–time graph is a straight line; this is its slope-intercept form.
conditions: Uniform acceleration along a straight line only.
units: u, v in m/s; a in m/s²; t in s

subject: physics
title: Displacement under uniform acceleration
explanation: Area under the velocity–time graph gives displacement: rectangle ut plus triangle ½at².
conditions: Straight-line motion with constant acceleration; s measured from the start point.
units: s in m; u in m/s; a in m/s²; t in s

subject: physics
title: Velocity–displacement relation
explanation: Eliminate time between v = u + at and s = ut + ½at²; the go-to equation when time is neither given nor asked.
conditions: Uniform acceleration along a straight line.
units: v, u in m/s; a in m/s²; s in m

subject: physics
title: Horizontal range of a projectile
explanation: Treat horizontal and vertical motion independently; R is maximum at θ = 45° (sin 2θ = 1) and complementary angles give equal range.
conditions: Launch and landing at the same horizontal level; no air resistance.
units: R in m; u in m/s; g in m/s²

subject: physics
title: Newton's second law
explanation: The net (resultant) of ALL forces on a body equals mass times acceleration; apply along each axis or along a chosen direction.
conditions: Valid in inertial frames; a is measured in an inertial frame.

subject: physics
title: Limiting friction
explanation: Static friction is self-adjusting (f ≤ μN) and reaches μN only at impending slip; kinetic friction is close to this limiting value once sliding starts.
conditions: At the point of impending sliding (static case); N is the normal reaction, not always mg.
units: f, N in newton; μ dimensionless

subject: physics
title: Banking of a road (frictionless)
explanation: The horizontal component of the normal reaction provides the centripetal force, so no friction is needed at exactly this speed.
conditions: Level circular turn of radius r, vehicle speed v, banking angle θ; ignore friction and tyre width.
units: v in m/s; r in m; θ in radians or degrees

subject: physics
title: Work–energy theorem
explanation: The total work of all forces (conservative and non-conservative) equals the change in kinetic energy — avoids resolving internal details.
conditions: Any motion in an inertial frame; W_net is work by the resultant force.
units: W in joule; KE in joule

subject: physics
title: Elastic potential energy of a spring
explanation: Energy stored when a spring is stretched or compressed by x from its natural length; the force is F = −kx (restoring).
conditions: Within the Hooke's-law (linear) region; x measured from natural length.
units: U in joule; k in N/m; x in m

subject: physics
title: Rotational Newton's second law
explanation: Net torque about a fixed axis equals moment of inertia times angular acceleration — the exact rotational analogue of F = ma.
conditions: Rotation about a fixed axis (or about the centre of mass); I and τ about the SAME axis.
units: τ in N·m; I in kg·m²; α in rad/s²

subject: physics
title: Parallel axis theorem
explanation: Shifts the moment of inertia from the centre-of-mass axis to any parallel axis a perpendicular distance d away.
conditions: One of the two parallel axes must pass through the centre of mass; d is the perpendicular distance between them.
units: I in kg·m²; M in kg; d in m

subject: physics
title: Rolling without slipping
explanation: The contact point is instantaneously at rest, so translation and rotation are locked; total KE = ½Mv² + ½Iω² evaluated about the centre of mass.
conditions: Pure rolling on a fixed surface; R is the body's radius.
units: v in m/s; ω in rad/s; R in m

subject: physics
title: Newton's law of gravitation
explanation: Every pair of masses attracts along the line joining them; for extended spherical bodies r is the centre-to-centre distance (shell theorem).
conditions: Point masses or uniformly spherical bodies; G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg².
units: F in newton; r in m; m in kg

subject: physics
title: Orbital velocity
explanation: Gravity supplies exactly the centripetal force for a circular orbit; independent of the orbiting body's mass.
conditions: Circular orbit of radius r measured from the CENTRE of the primary (mass M).

subject: physics
title: Escape velocity
explanation: Minimum launch speed to reach infinity with zero leftover speed (energy argument); for Earth vₑ = 11.2 km/s — independent of the projectile's mass and launch direction.
conditions: Negligible air resistance; only the primary's gravity acts after launch.

subject: physics
title: Kepler's third law
explanation: The square of the orbital period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis; M is the mass of the central body (same M for all planets around the Sun).
conditions: Bodies orbiting the same central mass M; a is the semi-major axis (radius for circular orbits).
units: T in s; a in m

subject: physics
title: Young's modulus
explanation: Ratio of longitudinal stress to longitudinal strain — the stiffness of the material, not the wire.
conditions: Within the elastic (Hooke's law) limit; uniform wire under axial tension or compression.

subject: physics
title: Terminal velocity (Stokes' law)
explanation: Viscous drag (6πηrv) grows with speed until it balances the net weight; then acceleration is zero. From Stokes' law with buoyancy included.
conditions: Small sphere, laminar flow (low Reynolds number), viscous medium of density σ and viscosity η.
units: v in m/s; r in m; η in Pa·s; ρ, σ in kg/m³

subject: physics
title: Bernoulli's equation
explanation: Energy conservation per unit volume along a streamline: pressure energy + kinetic energy + potential energy stays constant. Faster flow means lower pressure.
conditions: Steady, non-viscous, incompressible flow along one streamline of a fluid of density ρ.
units: P in Pa; v in m/s; h in m

subject: physics
title: First law of thermodynamics
explanation: Energy conservation with heat: heat supplied = rise in internal energy + work done BY the gas. In chemistry the same law is written ΔU = q + w (work done ON the gas is positive there).
conditions: Closed system; quasi-static processes let ΔW = ∫P dV be evaluated.

subject: physics
title: Isothermal work (ideal gas)
explanation: For a reversible isothermal expansion, W = ∫P dV with PV = nRT pulled out of the integral as constant.
conditions: Ideal gas, constant temperature (boiling contact with a reservoir), quasi-static process.
units: W in joule; T in kelvin

subject: physics
title: Carnot engine efficiency
explanation: The maximum possible efficiency of ANY engine working between two reservoirs; no real engine between the same temperatures can beat it.
conditions: Reversible engine between exactly two reservoirs; temperatures in kelvin (T₁ > T₂).

subject: physics
title: RMS speed of gas molecules
explanation: Depends only on temperature and (inverse) molar mass — lighter gases move faster at the same T.
conditions: Ideal gas; M in kg/mol with R, or m (mass of one molecule) with k_B. Average speed and most-probable speed are slightly smaller: v̄ = √(8RT/πM), v_p = √(2RT/M).
units: v in m/s; T in kelvin

subject: physics
title: Average translational kinetic energy
explanation: Per molecule, per degree of freedom ½k_BT; translational only. Depends purely on temperature — two different gases at the same T have the same mean translational KE.
conditions: Ideal gas; use with ½mv²̄ to find rms speed.
units: K in joule; T in kelvin

subject: physics
title: Period of a spring–mass oscillator
explanation: Independent of amplitude — the hallmark of SHM. For springs in series use 1/k = Σ1/kᵢ, in parallel k = Σkᵢ.
conditions: Massless ideal spring, frictionless horizontal/vertical motion; k = mω².
units: T in s; m in kg; k in N/m

subject: physics
title: Time period of a simple pendulum
explanation: For small swings the restoring torque is proportional to angular displacement, giving SHM; L is the distance from pivot to the centre of the bob.
conditions: Small amplitude (θ < 10° or so), light inextensible string, uniform g.
units: T in s; L in m; g in m/s²

subject: physics
title: Total energy in SHM
explanation: Constant in ideal SHM: all kinetic at the mean position, all potential at the extremes. E ∝ A².
conditions: Ideal (undamped) SHM with amplitude A; ω is the angular frequency.
units: E in joule; A in m; ω in rad/s

subject: physics
title: Speed of a wave on a stretched string
explanation: Tension provides the restoring force, mass per unit length μ the inertia; combined with v = fλ this gives the law of stretched strings.
conditions: Flexible string under uniform tension T (newton); μ in kg/m.

subject: physics
title: Coulomb's law
explanation: Inverse-square force between point charges; 1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C². For extended bodies integrate or use symmetry/Gauss.
conditions: Point charges (or uniformly charged spheres, with r centre-to-centre) in vacuum.
units: F in newton; q in coulomb; r in m

subject: physics
title: Gauss's law
explanation: Net electric flux through ANY closed surface equals enclosed charge / ε₀; field-line counting. Choose Gaussian surfaces matching the symmetry of E.
conditions: Any closed surface in vacuum; q_enc is the algebraic sum of charges INSIDE (external charges contribute zero net flux).
units: Φ in N·m²/C; q in coulomb

subject: physics
title: Parallel-plate capacitor
explanation: Field E = σ/ε₀ between plates is uniform, so V = Ed and C = Q/V gives the result; stored energy also equals ½QV = Q²/2C. With a dielectric, C → KC.
conditions: Plate separation d much smaller than plate size A (edge fringing ignored); vacuum (or multiply by K with dielectric).
units: C in farad; U in joule; d in m

subject: physics
title: Ohm's law
explanation: For metallic conductors at constant temperature, current is proportional to potential difference; R is the constant of proportionality.
conditions: Ohmic conductors at constant temperature; V–I graph is a straight line through the origin.
units: V in volt; I in ampere; R in ohm

subject: physics
title: Current and drift velocity
explanation: Current equals charge crossing a section per second; n is the free-electron density (≈ 10²⁹/m³ for metals), so even tiny v_d gives large I.
conditions: Conductor of cross-section A; e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C; drift is superimposed on random thermal motion.
units: I in ampere; n in m⁻³; v_d in m/s

subject: physics
title: Joule heating (power dissipated)
explanation: Use I²R when devices share current (series), V²/R when they share voltage (parallel); heat produced H = I²Rt.
conditions: Pure resistor; for AC use rms values; P is dissipated as heat.
units: P in watt; H in joule

subject: physics
title: Field of a long straight wire
explanation: From Ampère's circuital law for a wire treated as infinitely long; direction curls around the wire (right-hand thumb rule).
conditions: Wire length ≫ distance r from it; point not near the ends.
units: B in tesla; I in ampere; r in m; μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A

subject: physics
title: Lorentz force on a moving charge
explanation: Magnetic force is always ⟂ to v, so it changes direction but never speed and does no work; full form F = q(E + v × B).
conditions: Charge q moving with speed v at angle θ to B; force is maximum when v ⊥ B and zero when v ∥ B.
units: F in newton; q in coulomb; B in tesla

subject: physics
title: Faraday's law of induction
explanation: Induced EMF equals the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage; the minus sign is Lenz's law — induced effects oppose the change producing them.
conditions: Flux Φ = BA cos θ through N turns can change via B, A or orientation; valid for any circuit/rod configuration.
units: ε in volt; Φ in weber

subject: physics
title: Motional EMF
explanation: A rod of length l sliding with speed v perpendicular to B has its free charges pushed by qvB, creating an EMF across its ends; current I = Blv/R in a closed rail circuit.
conditions: Rod, velocity and field mutually perpendicular; more generally ε = Blv sin θ.
units: ε in volt; B in tesla; l, v in m, m/s

subject: physics
title: Resonance in a series LCR circuit
explanation: At resonance X_L = X_C so impedance is minimum (= R) and current is maximum; power factor cos φ = 1.
conditions: Series LCR driven by an AC source; off resonance the circuit is inductive (f > f₀) or capacitive (f < f₀).
units: ω in rad/s; f in hertz; L in henry; C in farad

subject: physics
title: Speed of electromagnetic waves
explanation: Maxwell's equations predict light as an EM wave travelling at c in vacuum; in a medium the speed becomes 1/√(με).
conditions: Free space (vacuum); also E₀/B₀ = c for the wave's field amplitudes.

subject: physics
title: Thin lens formula
explanation: Positions of object and image for a thin lens; magnification m = v/u (sign included). Combining lenses in contact: 1/f = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂.
conditions: Thin lens in air with the Cartesian sign convention: distances measured from the optical centre, against the incident light direction negative; real object u < 0.
units: u, v, f in m (or consistent units)

subject: physics
title: Lensmaker's formula
explanation: Relates focal length to refractive index n (relative to the surrounding medium) and the radii of curvature of the two surfaces.
conditions: Thin lens; R₁, R₂ carry Cartesian signs; if the outside medium is not air, replace (n − 1) by (n_lens/n_medium − 1).
units: f, R in m; n dimensionless

subject: physics
title: Critical angle for total internal reflection
explanation: At the critical angle the refracted ray grazes the interface (90°); beyond it light is totally reflected back into the denser medium.
conditions: Light going from denser to rarer medium; n is the refractive index of the denser medium relative to the rarer one.
units: C in degrees or radians; n dimensionless

subject: physics
title: Fringe width in Young's double slit
explanation: Equally spaced bright/dark fringes; fringe width grows with screen distance D and wavelength λ, shrinks with slit separation d.
conditions: D ≫ d, small angles, coherent sources; in a medium replace λ by λ/n (fringes come closer).
units: β, D, d in m; λ in m (or nm)

subject: physics
title: Malus's law
explanation: Intensity transmitted by an analyser whose axis makes angle θ with the polarised light's plane; unpolarised light through a polariser loses half (I₀/2).
conditions: Plane-polarised light of intensity I₀ incident on the analyser; θ = angle between the two transmission axes.
units: I in W/m²; θ in degrees or radians

subject: physics
title: Einstein's photoelectric equation
explanation: One photon of energy hν ejects one electron: part of the energy pays the work function φ₀, the rest appears as maximum kinetic energy (= eV₀ stopping potential).
conditions: ν above threshold ν₀ = φ₀/h; emission is instantaneous and independent of intensity (intensity only sets photocurrent).
units: hν, φ₀ in joule or eV; KE_max in joule or eV

subject: physics
title: de Broglie wavelength
explanation: Matter waves: the same relation as photons. An electron accelerated through V volts has λ ≈ 1.227/√V nm.
conditions: Non-relativistic speeds for the λ = h/mv form; use p = √(2m·eV) for accelerated charged particles.
units: λ in m; p in kg·m/s; h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s

subject: physics
title: Bohr energy levels
explanation: Hydrogen-like species (H, He⁺, Li²⁺…); the negative sign means the electron is bound. Transitions give E_photon = E_i − E_f.
conditions: Single-electron (hydrogen-like) atoms/ions of nuclear charge Z; n = 1, 2, 3… Bohr radius rₙ = 0.529 n²/Z Å.

subject: physics
title: Rydberg formula (hydrogen spectrum)
explanation: Wavelengths of all hydrogen spectral lines: Lyman (n₁ = 1, UV), Balmer (n₁ = 2, visible), Paschen (n₁ = 3, IR).
conditions: Hydrogen atom emission; n₂ > n₁; R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹ (Rydberg constant).
units: λ in m; R in m⁻¹

subject: physics
title: Binding energy from mass defect
explanation: The mass defect Δm (sum of nucleon masses − nuclear mass) converts to binding energy via E = Δmc²; 1 u c² = 931.5 MeV.
conditions: Δm expressed in atomic mass units (u); BE/nucleon peaks near iron (≈ 8.8 MeV) — the reason fusion and fission both release energy.
units: E_b in MeV; Δm in u

subject: physics
title: Transistor current gains
explanation: Common-emitter gain β is typically 20–200; α is slightly below 1. They satisfy I_E = I_B + I_C and β = α/(1 − α).
conditions: Transistor in active region; α = α_dc defined with collector and emitter currents.
units: β, α dimensionless; currents in ampere

subject: chemistry
title: Number of moles
explanation: Moles connect mass to number of particles: n = m/M = N/N_A with N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
conditions: M is molar mass in g/mol (numerically equal to molecular mass in u).
units: n in mol; m in g; M in g/mol

subject: chemistry
title: Molarity
explanation: Moles of solute per litre of SOLUTION (not solvent); for dilution problems use M₁V₁ = M₂V₂.
conditions: Temperature must be quoted, since volume changes with T. Use molality (m = n/mass of solvent in kg) when T changes.

subject: chemistry
title: Heisenberg uncertainty principle
explanation: Position and momentum of a microscopic particle cannot both be known exactly at the same time; h/4π = 5.27 × 10⁻³⁵ J·s.
conditions: Significant only for microscopic particles (electrons, atoms); negligible for macroscopic bodies because h is tiny.
units: Δx in m; Δp in kg·m/s

subject: chemistry
title: Bond order (molecular orbital theory)
explanation: Half the difference of bonding and antibonding electrons; higher bond order means shorter, stronger bonds. O₂ has B.O. = 2 and is paramagnetic (two unpaired electrons in π*).
conditions: MOT of diatomics: B.O. = 0 (e.g. He₂) means the molecule does not exist; half-integral or odd-electron species are paramagnetic.

subject: chemistry
title: HF is a liquid, HCl is a gas
explanation: HF molecules associate through strong hydrogen bonding (H attached to small, highly electronegative F), so much more energy is needed to separate them. HCl, HBr, HI show only weak dipole–dipole/dispersion forces and are gases.
conditions: Classic example of H-bonding raising boiling point; similar logic explains the anomalous boiling points of H₂O and NH₃ within their groups.

subject: chemistry
title: Ideal gas equation
explanation: Combines Boyle's, Charles' and Avogadro's laws; R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ = 0.0821 L·atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
conditions: High temperature and low pressure (negligible molecular volume and interactions); real gases deviate otherwise.
units: P in Pa (or atm); V in m³ (or L); T in kelvin

subject: chemistry
title: van der Waals equation (real gases)
explanation: Corrects ideal-gas behaviour: a measures attractive intermolecular forces (pressure correction), b accounts for the finite volume of molecules.
conditions: Real gases, especially at high pressure / low temperature; He and H₂ have very small a because attraction is weak.
units: a in atm·L²/mol²; b in L/mol

subject: chemistry
title: Graham's law of diffusion/effusion
explanation: Rate of effusion is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass — lighter gases escape/diffuse faster.
conditions: Same temperature and pressure; r can be measured as volume/time or moles/time.
units: r in mL/s or mol/s; M in g/mol

subject: chemistry
title: First law of thermodynamics (chemistry convention)
explanation: Internal energy change = heat supplied to the system + work done ON the system. Physics texts write ΔQ = ΔU + ΔW — the SAME law with work by the gas positive instead.
conditions: Closed system; for reversible expansion w = −nRT ln(V_f/V_i), for irreversible expansion against constant external pressure w = −p_ext ΔV.

subject: chemistry
title: Enthalpy–internal energy relation
explanation: For gas-phase reactions H = U + PV, so the two state functions differ by the PV change; ΔH is heat at constant pressure, ΔU heat at constant volume.
conditions: Ideal gases; Δn_g = (moles of gaseous products) − (moles of gaseous reactants). If Δn_g = 0 then ΔH = ΔU.
units: H, U in kJ/mol; R in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; T in kelvin

subject: chemistry
title: Gibbs energy and spontaneity
explanation: At constant T and P the process is spontaneous when ΔG < 0 and at equilibrium when ΔG = 0; also ΔG° = −RT ln K.
conditions: Constant temperature and pressure; ΔG° = 0 at equilibrium, so ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q with Q < K meaning forward-spontaneous.
units: G, H in kJ/mol; S in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹; T in kelvin

subject: chemistry
title: Equilibrium constant Kc
explanation: For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD at equilibrium, the ratio of product to reactant molar concentrations (each to its stoichiometric power) is constant at a given T.
conditions: Aqueous/gaseous species only — pure solids and pure liquids have activity 1 and are omitted; Kc is temperature dependent.

subject: chemistry
title: Relation between Kp and Kc
explanation: Converts between pressure and concentration equilibrium constants for gaseous reactions; use R = 0.0821 L·atm to match atm units.
conditions: Ideal gases; Δn_g = (moles gaseous products) − (moles gaseous reactants); if Δn_g = 0 then Kp = Kc.

subject: chemistry
title: pH of a solution
explanation: Logarithmic acidity scale; at 25 °C pure water has [H⁺] = [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁷ M so pH = 7 and pH + pOH = 14.
conditions: Aqueous solutions, 25 °C for the neutral value 7; Kw = [H⁺][OH⁻] = 10⁻¹⁴ at 25 °C.

subject: chemistry
title: Henderson–Hasselbalch equation (buffer pH)
explanation: pH of an acidic buffer (weak acid + its salt); for a basic buffer pOH = pKb + log[salt]/[base]. Best buffering capacity lies within pKa ± 1.
conditions: Weak acid + conjugate base (e.g. CH₃COOH/CH₃COONa); for pH = pKa the acid:salt ratio must be 1:1.
units: pH, pKa dimensionless; concentrations in mol/L

subject: chemistry
title: Ksp of an A2B3-type salt
explanation: For A₂B₃ ⇌ 2A³⁺ + 3B²⁻ with molar solubility S: Ksp = (2S)²(3S)³ = 108 S⁵. Similarly AB₂ type gives Ksp = 4S³ and simple AB gives S².
conditions: Sparingly soluble salt in pure water at the stated temperature; no common ion present.

subject: chemistry
title: Nernst equation (298 K)
explanation: Cell potential under non-standard concentrations; 0.059 ≈ 2.303RT/F at 298 K. The cell is spontaneous while E_cell > 0.
conditions: 298 K; n = electrons transferred in the balanced cell reaction; Q = reaction quotient of that reaction.

subject: chemistry
title: Cell potential and Gibbs energy
explanation: Standard Gibbs change of the cell reaction; a positive standard EMF means a negative ΔG° and a spontaneous cell reaction. Also gives log K_c = nE°/0.059.
conditions: Standard conditions (1 M, 1 bar, 298 K); F = 96500 C/mol; ΔG° in J when F is used.
units: ΔG° in J/mol; E° in volt

subject: chemistry
title: Faraday's first law of electrolysis
explanation: Mass deposited is proportional to charge passed: m = ZIt with Z = E/F; E is equivalent weight = M/(n-factor).
conditions: Electrolysis with current I (ampere) flowing for t seconds; n-factor = electrons per ion (Cu²⁺ → Cu gives E = M/2).
units: m in g; I in ampere; t in s; F = 96500 C/mol

subject: chemistry
title: First-order rate constant
explanation: Integrated rate law for first-order decay (radioactivity, many decompositions); a ln/[A]₀ vs t plot is a straight line with slope −k.
conditions: First order ONLY; [A]₀ initial concentration, [A] at time t; k has units of time⁻¹.
units: k in s⁻¹; concentrations any consistent unit

subject: chemistry
title: Half-life of a first-order reaction
explanation: Independent of the initial concentration — a unique fingerprint of first order (0.693 = ln 2). For zero order t½ = [A]₀/2k.
conditions: First-order kinetics only; each successive half-life takes the SAME time.
units: t½ in s; k in s⁻¹

subject: chemistry
title: Arrhenius equation
explanation: Rate constant rises steeply with temperature; the log form log k = log A − E_a/(2.303RT) gives E_a from a log k vs 1/T plot (slope = −E_a/2.303R).
conditions: E_a = activation energy (J/mol); A = frequency factor; valid for the temperature range studied.
units: k in s⁻¹ (first order); E_a in J/mol

subject: chemistry
title: Raoult's law (volatile binary mixture)
explanation: Partial pressure of each component equals its pure vapour pressure times mole fraction; total pressure is their sum — a straight line versus composition.
conditions: Ideal solutions (similar molecules, e.g. benzene + toluene); positive deviations mean stronger A–B repulsion (higher vapour pressure).
units: p in mmHg or atm; x dimensionless

subject: chemistry
title: Depression of freezing point
explanation: A colligative property: the freezing point drops in proportion to molality; Kf (cryoscopic constant) = 1.86 K·kg/mol for water. Boiling point elevation is analogous: ΔTb = i Kb m.
conditions: Dilute, non-volatile solute; i = van't Hoff factor (i = 1 for non-electrolytes, ≈ 2 for NaCl, ≈ 3 for CaCl₂ assuming full dissociation).
units: ΔTf in K; m in mol/kg; Kf in K·kg/mol

subject: chemistry
title: Copper with dilute nitric acid
explanation: Dilute HNO₃ is reduced to colourless NO (which turns brown in air as NO₂ forms); concentrated acid instead gives brown NO₂ fumes.
conditions: Cold dilute HNO₃; NO is a colourless gas that oxidises to brown NO₂ on contact with air.

subject: chemistry
title: Copper with concentrated nitric acid
explanation: Concentrated HNO₃ is a strong oxidant, reduced directly to brown NO₂; the solution turns blue-green due to Cu²⁺.
conditions: Concentrated (≈ 68%) nitric acid; distinguishes it from the dilute acid case which liberates NO.

subject: chemistry
title: Iodometric titration of hypo
explanation: Sodium thiosulphate ('hypo') reduces iodine to iodide, itself oxidised to tetrathionate; the standard end point is the disappearance of the blue starch–iodine colour.
conditions: Neutral or mildly acidic medium; basis of iodometric estimation of oxidants (KMnO₄, K₂Cr₂O₇, Cu²⁺) via liberated I₂.

subject: chemistry
title: Lithium forms a stable nitride
explanation: Lithium is the ONLY alkali metal that combines directly with N₂ to give a stable nitride — part of its diagonal relationship with magnesium (Mg also forms Mg₃N₂).
conditions: Direct combination of the metal with nitrogen; Li also forms normal oxide Li₂O (not peroxide) when burnt in oxygen.

subject: chemistry
title: Alkali metal oxides: peroxide vs superoxide
explanation: Li burns to normal oxide (Li₂O), Na forms peroxide Na₂O₂, while K, Rb and Cs form superoxides MO₂ — the bigger cation stabilises the bigger superoxide ion.
conditions: Burning the metal in excess oxygen; KO₂ is paramagnetic and used in breathing masks (releases O₂ with CO₂ absorption).

subject: chemistry
title: Permanganate reduction in acidic medium
explanation: E° ≈ 1.51 V: purple MnO₄⁻ is reduced to nearly colourless Mn²⁺ by 5 electrons — the half reaction behind KMnO₄ titrations (Fe²⁺, oxalate, H₂O₂).
conditions: Acidic medium (dilute H₂SO₄); in neutral/alkaline medium MnO₄⁻ instead goes to brown MnO₂ precipitate.

subject: chemistry
title: CFSE of an octahedral complex
explanation: t₂g orbitals are stabilised by 0.4Δo each, e_g destabilised by 0.6Δo; high-spin d⁵ (e.g. Mn²⁺ with weak-field ligands) gives CFSE = 0.
conditions: Octahedral field; pairing energy P decides high-spin vs low-spin when d⁴–d⁷. For tetrahedral fields Δt ≈ (4/9)Δo with the level order reversed.
units: Δo, CFSE in cm⁻¹ or kJ/mol

subject: chemistry
title: Prussian blue test for Fe3+
explanation: Ferric ion with potassium ferrocyanide gives the deep blue iron(III) ferrocyanide (Prussian blue); Fe²⁺ instead gives Turnbull's blue with ferricyanide.
conditions: Group III cations (after removing Groups I–II); the deep blue colouration is confirmed only in cold, dilute solution.

subject: chemistry
title: Ionization energy anomalies
explanation: Half-filled (N: 2p³) and fully-filled (Be: 2s², Mg: 3s²) subshells are extra stable, so removing an electron from the NEXT element actually needs less energy despite higher nuclear charge.
conditions: First ionization energies compared within a period; similar anomalies: P > S in period 3.

subject: chemistry
title: Inductive (-I) strength order
explanation: Electron-withdrawing power falls down the list; the −I effect decays with distance from the functional group and stabilises negative charge while destabilising positive charge.
conditions: Compare substituents attached through the SAME atom; halogen −I order (F > Cl > Br > I) follows electronegativity, opposite to their +M order.

subject: chemistry
title: Carbocation stability order
explanation: Hyperconjugation and the +I effect of alkyl groups disperse the positive charge; free radicals follow the same order. Carbanions are the REVERSE (3° < 2° < 1°) since alkyl groups destabilise negative charge.
conditions: Stability comparisons of simple alkyl species; aryl/benzyl carbocations are further stabilised by resonance.

subject: chemistry
title: Huckel's rule for aromaticity
explanation: A species is aromatic when cyclic, planar, fully conjugated AND carrying (4n + 2) π electrons (n = 0, 1, 2 …). Benzene: 6 π electrons (n = 1); cyclobutadiene's 4 π electrons (4n) is antiaromatic.
conditions: All three structural requirements must hold simultaneously; examples: pyridine (6 π, aromatic), tropylium cation (6 π, aromatic).

subject: chemistry
title: Markovnikov addition
explanation: H adds to the doubly-bonded carbon already carrying more H atoms, because the reaction proceeds through the more stable (more substituted) carbocation.
conditions: Ionic addition of HX to an unsymmetrical alkene, no peroxides present.

subject: chemistry
title: Peroxide (anti-Markovnikov) effect
explanation: Peroxides generate free radicals, reversing the regiochemistry: Br attaches to give the more stable RADICAL intermediate.
conditions: Works ONLY with HBr; the chain energetics fail for HCl and HI, which still add normally (Markovnikov).

subject: chemistry
title: Friedel–Crafts alkylation
explanation: Anhydrous AlCl₃ generates the electrophile (CH₃⁺-like) which substitutes H on the ring; polyalkylation can occur because products are MORE activated than benzene.
conditions: Anhydrous Lewis acid catalyst, dry conditions; fails when the ring carries strongly deactivating (–NO₂) or basic amino groups.

subject: chemistry
title: Hydrolysis of haloalkanes
explanation: Aqueous KOH substitutes –OH for the halogen (nucleophilic substitution); primary halides go via SN2, tertiary via SN1.
conditions: Aqueous (not alcoholic) alkali, warm; contrast with alcoholic KOH which ELIMINATES to give an alkene.

subject: chemistry
title: Dehydrohalogenation
explanation: Alcoholic KOH removes a β-hydrogen together with the halogen to give an alkene (elimination, E2); this is the standard lab preparation of ethene.
conditions: Alcoholic KOH and heat; the substrate must have at least one β-hydrogen.

subject: chemistry
title: Saytzeff (Zaitsev) rule
explanation: Elimination preferentially forms the MORE substituted alkene (but-2-ene > but-1-ene) because it is more stable; bulky bases can instead follow Hofmann selectivity.
conditions: β-elimination from a secondary/tertiary halide; product quoted as the major alkene.

subject: chemistry
title: Grignard reagent formation
explanation: Mg inserts into the C–X bond giving a strongly polarised Cδ−–Mgδ+ reagent — a versatile carbon nucleophile for building C–C bonds (with carbonyls, CO₂, nitriles).
conditions: Absolutely dry ether and moisture-free glassware; water or any protic solvent destroys it (gives the alkane).

subject: chemistry
title: Lucas test (alcohol classification)
explanation: ZnCl₂ (a Lewis acid) speeds up substitution; tertiary alcohols cloud the reagent immediately, secondary in ~5 minutes, primary only on heating.
conditions: Room temperature, anhydrous Lucas reagent (conc. HCl + ZnCl₂); turbidity = insoluble alkyl chloride separating out.

subject: chemistry
title: Reimer–Tiemann reaction
explanation: Phenol + CHCl₃/NaOH places a –CHO ortho to the –OH, giving salicylaldehyde; the attacking electrophile is dichlorocarbene (:CCl₂) generated by strong base.
conditions: Aqueous NaOH, then acidification; works because phenoxide activates the ring — ordinary alcohols do not undergo it.

subject: chemistry
title: Fehling's test
explanation: Cu²⁺ (blue) is reduced to red Cu₂O by aliphatic aldehydes; aromatic aldehydes such as benzaldehyde do NOT respond.
conditions: Fehling A + Fehling B freshly mixed, warmed; aldehydes without steric hindrance reduce it (α-hydroxy ketones also positive).

subject: chemistry
title: Tollens' silver mirror test
explanation: Ammoniacal Ag⁺ is reduced to metallic silver — a mirror on the wall of the tube; responds to ALL aldehydes (unlike Fehling) and α-hydroxy ketones like glucose.
conditions: Freshly prepared Tollens' reagent, gentle warming in a clean tube.

subject: chemistry
title: Cannizzaro reaction
explanation: Aldehydes WITHOUT an α-hydrogen disproportionate in concentrated base: one molecule is reduced to the alcohol, the other oxidised to the carboxylate.
conditions: No α-H on the aldehyde (HCHO, benzaldehyde, 2,2-dimethylpropanal) and concentrated alkali.

subject: chemistry
title: Haloform (iodoform) reaction
explanation: Methyl ketones are halogenated at the α-carbon until the group cleaves, giving yellow CHI₃ with its characteristic antiseptic smell; ethanol and secondary alcohols with a CH₃–CH(OH)– group also give it.
conditions: I₂/NaOH; positive for CH₃CO– (methyl ketones) and CH₃CH(OH)– species only.

subject: chemistry
title: Carbylamine reaction
explanation: Primary amines (only) react with chloroform and alkali to give foul-smelling isocyanides — the classic distinction test for 1° amines.
conditions: Alcoholic KOH, warm; secondary and tertiary amines do not respond.

subject: chemistry
title: Hofmann bromamide degradation
explanation: An amide is converted by Br2/NaOH to a primary amine containing ONE CARBON LESS than the amide — the reliable chain-shortening route.
conditions: Bromine in concentrated aqueous/alcoholic NaOH, warm; the mechanism proceeds through a nitrene intermediate.

subject: chemistry
title: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis
explanation: Potassium phthalimide is alkylated, then hydrolysed to give a PURE primary amine (no 2 degree/3 degree mixture) — best with primary alkyl halides.
conditions: Alkyl halides (SN2), not aryl halides; final step hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis of the N-alkylphthalimide.

subject: chemistry
title: Peptide bond formation
explanation: Two amino acids condense: the -COOH of one and the -NH2 of the next release water and form the amide (peptide) link — the backbone of every protein.
conditions: Condensation (often enzyme-catalysed in vivo); hydrolysis of the bond reverses it during digestion.

subject: chemistry
title: Nylon-6,6 condensation
explanation: Adipic acid (HOOC-(CH2)4-COOH) and hexamethylenediamine (H2N-(CH2)6-NH2) condense through this amidation at high temperature and pressure; the 6,6 counts the carbons in each monomer.
conditions: 1:1 monomer ratio (as in the nylon rope trick); condensation polymerisation — water is eliminated as each amide bond forms.

subject: chemistry
title: Aspirin synthesis
explanation: Salicylic acid is acetylated by acetic anhydride to give acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin), an analgesic and antipyretic that also inhibits platelet aggregation.
conditions: Acid catalyst, anhydrous conditions; acetic anhydride (not acetic acid) drives the reaction to completion.

subject: mathematics
title: Number of subsets of a set
explanation: A set with n elements has 2^n subsets (each element is either in or out); proper subsets = 2^n − 1, and the number of relations from A (m elements) to B (n elements) is 2^(mn).
conditions: n = number of distinct elements; includes the empty set and the set itself.

subject: mathematics
title: Euler's formula
explanation: Links exponentials and trigonometry; multiplying a complex number by e^{iθ} rotates it by angle θ. Special case: e^{iπ} + 1 = 0.
conditions: θ in radians; the bridge between polar and exponential forms z = re^{iθ}.

subject: mathematics
title: De Moivre's theorem
explanation: Powers of unit complex numbers rotate the angle; used to derive multiple-angle identities and to find all n-th roots of a complex number (arguments spaced 2π/n).
conditions: n is an integer (rational n needs care with multiple values); equivalent to (e^{iθ})ⁿ = e^{inθ}.

subject: mathematics
title: Cube roots of unity
explanation: ω = −½ + i√3/2 and ω² = ω̄ = −½ − i√3/2; any power of ω reduces to one of {1, ω, ω²}.
conditions: ω is a non-real (primitive) cube root of unity; |ω| = 1 and arg ω = 2π/3.

subject: mathematics
title: Inverse of a matrix via adjoint
explanation: adj(A) is the transpose of the cofactor matrix; note the order swap for products: (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹ and (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ.
conditions: det A ≠ 0 (invertible/singular check); always verify A·adj(A) = (det A)I.

subject: mathematics
title: Cayley–Hamilton theorem (2x2)
explanation: Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation; multiply by A⁻¹ to express A⁻¹ in terms of A and I — the trick behind 'find A⁻¹/A⁴ from A²' questions.
conditions: Square matrices; for any n, higher powers reduce to combinations of lower powers using the characteristic polynomial.

subject: mathematics
title: Permutations (arrangements)
explanation: Ordered selections of r out of n distinct objects; nPr = n(n−1)(n−2)…(n−r+1) falls from n, r times.
conditions: All objects distinct, no repetition; with repetition allowed: nʳ arrangements.

subject: mathematics
title: Combinations (selections)
explanation: Unordered selections; Pascal's rule ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₋₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ builds Pascal's triangle; ⁿCᵣ = (n/r)·ⁿ⁻¹Cᵣ₋₁ is useful for fast evaluation.
conditions: Distinct objects; e.g. choosing r from n when order is irrelevant; also counts diagonals of an n-gon: nC2 − n.

subject: mathematics
title: Circular permutations
explanation: n distinct objects around a circle: fix one to break rotational symmetry, leaving (n−1)!; if clockwise/anticlockwise arrangements are identical (necklace, garland), divide by 2.
conditions: All objects distinct; rotations counted as the same arrangement.

subject: mathematics
title: General term of (a + b)^n
explanation: The (r+1)th term of the expansion; the rth term from the END equals the (n−r+2)th from the start. For (x − a)ⁿ, attach (−1)ʳ.
conditions: r = 0, 1, …, n; positive integer n for the finite expansion.

subject: mathematics
title: Sum of binomial coefficients
explanation: Put a = b = 1 in (1 + 1)ⁿ; similarly (1 − 1)ⁿ gives that the sum of even-indexed coefficients equals the odd-indexed sum = 2ⁿ⁻¹.
conditions: n a positive integer; the generating trick: set x = 1, −1, i in (1 + x)ⁿ.

subject: mathematics
title: Arithmetic progression (AP)
explanation: Constant difference d between consecutive terms; S_n = n × (average of first and last terms). If aₚ = q and a_q = p, then d = −1 and the (p+q)th term is 0.
conditions: d common; n is the term number.

subject: mathematics
title: Geometric progression (GP)
explanation: Constant ratio r; the infinite sum exists only for |r| < 1. For three terms prefer a/r, a, ar; GM² = AM × HM connects the three classical means.
conditions: S_n formula needs r ≠ 1; S_∞ needs |r| < 1.

subject: mathematics
title: Special sums (first powers, squares, cubes)
explanation: Sum of cubes equals the SQUARE of the sum of first powers (Nicomachus); k runs 1 to n.
conditions: k = 1, 2, …, n; n a positive integer.

subject: mathematics
title: The sine limit
explanation: x must be in RADIANS; companion limits: tan x/x → 1, (1 − cos x)/x → 0, (1 − cos x)/x² → 1/2.
conditions: x → 0 with x measured in radians; standard tool for evaluating 0/0 trig limits.

subject: mathematics
title: Exponential and logarithmic limits
explanation: Companion: (aˣ − 1)/x → ln a; both are the derivatives of eˣ and ln x at 0 in disguise.
conditions: x → 0; general form (e^{kx} − 1)/x → k.

subject: mathematics
title: The e limit
explanation: Equivalently lim (1 + 1/n)ⁿ = e as n → ∞; the definition of continuous compounding. Handle 1^∞ indeterminate forms by converting to this shape.
conditions: The base tends to 1 while the exponent tends to ∞ (1^∞ form); take logarithm to reduce to a product.

subject: mathematics
title: Second derivative test
explanation: f''(c) > 0 gives a local minimum; if f''(c) = 0 the test is inconclusive — fall back to sign changes of f' (first derivative test).
conditions: f twice differentiable near c with f'(c) = 0; for absolute extrema on [a, b] also compare endpoint values.

subject: mathematics
title: Linear approximation (differentials)
explanation: The tangent line as a local approximation — used to estimate values like √25.3 or (0.998)⁵ by choosing a convenient nearby x.
conditions: δx small compared with the scale over which f' changes; f differentiable at x.

subject: mathematics
title: Related rates (chain rule)
explanation: Rates connect through the intermediate variable; classic setups: balloon (V = 4/3 πr³), ladder sliding, cone-shaped tank with similar triangles.
conditions: Differentiable relation between the quantities; write the geometric relation FIRST, then differentiate with respect to t.
units: units of V per unit time

subject: mathematics
title: Standard inverse-trigonometric integrals
explanation: Memorise with their derivatives; related: ∫dx/√(x² + a²) = ln|x + √(x² + a²)| + C and ∫dx/(x² − a²) = (1/2a)ln|(x−a)/(x+a)| + C.
conditions: a > 0; the arcsin form needs |x| < a.

subject: mathematics
title: The e^x (f + f') integral
explanation: Spot f + f′ in the integrand and the answer is immediate; e.g. ∫eˣ(tan x + sec²x)dx = eˣ tan x + C.
conditions: f differentiable; the integrand must separate exactly into the eˣ[f + f′] pattern.

subject: mathematics
title: Integration by parts
explanation: Choose u by the ILATE priority: Inverse trig, Log, Algebraic, Trig, Exponential — the one EARLIER in ILATE becomes u; e.g. ∫x eˣ dx = eˣ(x − 1) + C.
conditions: Both factors differentiable; applies to ∫ln x dx = x ln x − x + C as well.

subject: mathematics
title: King's property of definite integrals
explanation: Replace x by a + b − x, then ADD the two forms — often the only way to crack ∫ f(x)/(1 + f(x)) patterns over symmetric limits.
conditions: Any integrable f on [a, b]; especially powerful combined with x → −x symmetry.

subject: mathematics
title: Odd and even functions over symmetric limits
formula: $\int_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = 0\ \text{if } f \text{ odd};\quad = 2\int_0^a f(x)\,dx\ \text{if } f \text{ even}$
explanation: Check parity before integrating anything over [−a, a]; saves the entire computation for odd integrands.
conditions: Symmetric limits; f(−x) = −f(x) (odd) or f(−x) = f(x) (even).

subject: mathematics
title: Integrating factor (linear ODE)
explanation: For dy/dx + Py = Q (P, Q functions of x), multiplying by the integrating factor makes the left side an exact derivative d/dx[y·I.F.].
conditions: The equation must be LINEAR with leading coefficient 1; if x is the dependent variable, swap roles of x and y.

subject: mathematics
title: Section formula
explanation: Point dividing the join of (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) in the ratio m : n internally; midpoint is the special case m = n. External division flips a sign: ((mx₂ − nx₁)/(m−n), …).
conditions: Ratio m : n taken from the FIRST point toward the second for internal division; m + n ≠ 0 for external division.

subject: mathematics
title: Distance of a point from a line
explanation: Perpendicular distance from (x₁, y₁) to ax + by + c = 0; the same numerator at two parallel lines gives the distance between them: |c₁ − c₂|/√(a² + b²).
conditions: Line must be in the standard form with (a, b) ≠ (0, 0); works for both sides of the line (absolute value).

subject: mathematics
title: Distance between parallel lines
explanation: For ax + by + c₁ = 0 and ax + by + c₂ = 0 — the SAME a and b (normalise coefficients first if they differ by a factor).
conditions: Coefficients of x and y must be identical in both equations.

subject: mathematics
title: Circle: general equation
explanation: Centre (−g, −f), radius r = √(g² + f² − c); a REAL circle needs g² + f² − c > 0. Completing the square converts any valid circle equation to this form.
conditions: Coefficients of x² and y² equal AND no xy term; radius real requires g² + f² > c.
units: g, f, c in length/length² units

subject: mathematics
title: Length of tangent from an external point
explanation: From point (x₁, y₁) to the circle S = x² + y² + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0, the tangent length is √S₁ where S₁ is the circle expression evaluated at the point; real only if the point is outside.
conditions: Point must be ON or OUTSIDE the circle (S₁ ≥ 0); both tangent segments from an external point are equal.

subject: mathematics
title: Condition for tangency (line and circle)
explanation: The line y = mx + c touches the circle x² + y² = a² exactly when the perpendicular distance from the centre equals the radius; solving together gives a discriminant of zero.
conditions: Circle centred at the origin; equivalently the distance from (0, 0) to the line is a.

subject: mathematics
title: Standard parabola y^2 = 4ax
explanation: Focus (a, 0), directrix x = −a; parametric point (at², 2at); latus rectum length 4a. Sister forms: x² = 4ay (opens up), y² = −4ax (opens left).
conditions: Vertex at origin, axis along x, a > 0; the focal distance of (x, y) is x + a.
units: a, x, y in length units

subject: mathematics
title: Standard ellipse
explanation: Foci (±ae, 0), directrices x = ±a/e, sum of focal distances = 2a; eccentricity 0 < e < 1 (e = 0 would be a circle).
conditions: a > b > 0 with major axis along x; if b > a the foci move to the y-axis and the roles swap.

subject: mathematics
title: Standard hyperbola
explanation: Foci (±ae, 0); |difference of focal distances| = 2a; asymptotes y = ±(b/a)x; eccentricity e > 1. Rectangular (equilateral) hyperbola: a = b.
conditions: e > 1 with transverse axis along x; conjugate hyperbola swaps the minus sign.

subject: mathematics
title: Focal chord of a parabola
explanation: Chord through the focus joining the points with parameters t and −1/t; its minimum length is 4a — the latus rectum (at t = 1).
conditions: Parabola y² = 4ax with parametrisation (at², 2at); endpoints must be focal.

subject: mathematics
title: Direction cosines identity
explanation: l = cos α, m = cos β, n = cos γ with α + β + γ related angles to the axes; direction RATIOS are proportional to (l, m, n) and need not satisfy this.
conditions: Direction cosines of a single directed line; direction ratios are any triple proportional to them.

subject: mathematics
title: Angle between two 3D lines
explanation: (a₁, a₂, a₃) and (b₁, b₂, b₃) are direction ratios of the lines; numerator zero means perpendicular, proportional triples mean parallel.
conditions: Use the absolute value for the acute angle between lines.

subject: mathematics
title: Plane in intercept form
explanation: The plane cuts intercepts a, b, c on the x-, y-, z-axes; general form ax + by + cz + d = 0 converts by dividing by −d.
conditions: None of a, b, c is zero (the plane misses no axis); planes through the origin have no intercept form.
units: a, b, c in length units

subject: mathematics
title: Dot (scalar) product
explanation: Commutative and distributive; a·b = 0 ⟺ nonzero vectors are perpendicular. In component form a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃; work done = F·d.
conditions: θ is the angle between the vectors when placed tail-to-tail (0 ≤ θ ≤ π).

subject: mathematics
title: Cross (vector) product
explanation: Magnitude equals the area of the parallelogram spanned by the vectors; direction by the right-hand rule; a × b = 0 ⟺ parallel (nonzero) vectors. Triangle area = ½|a × b|.
conditions: Anti-commutative: b × a = −(a × b); not defined in 2D without embedding.

subject: mathematics
title: Scalar triple product
formula: $[\vec a\ \vec b\ \vec c] = \vec a \cdot (\vec b \times \vec c)$
explanation: Gives the (signed) volume of the parallelepiped; coplanar vectors ⟺ [a b c] = 0. Tetrahedron volume = (1/6)|[a b c]|. Swapping two vectors flips the sign; cyclic rotation preserves it.
conditions: Volume is the ABSOLUTE value; a determinant expansion computes it in components.

subject: mathematics
title: Variance (computational form)
explanation: Mean of squares minus square of the mean — the fastest hand computation; standard deviation σ is its positive square root and shares the data's units.
conditions: Ungrouped data; for frequency distributions use Σfᵢxᵢ²/N − (Σfᵢxᵢ/N)². Adding a constant to every observation leaves σ unchanged.

subject: mathematics
title: Addition rule of probability
explanation: For mutually exclusive events P(A ∩ B) = 0, so the probabilities simply add; for three events add back the triple intersection after subtracting pairwise ones.
conditions: Any two events on the same sample space; complements give P(A') = 1 − P(A).

subject: mathematics
title: Conditional probability
explanation: Restricting the sample space to B; independence is exactly P(A|B) = P(A) (equivalently P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B)).
conditions: P(B) > 0; Bayes' theorem is built from two conditional probabilities.

subject: mathematics
title: Bayes' theorem
explanation: Reverses conditioning: from causes E₁, …, Eₙ partitioning the sample space, it updates to the probability that cause Eᵢ produced the observed A.
conditions: E₁, …, Eₙ must partition the sample space (mutually exclusive, exhaustive); each P(Eₖ) > 0.

subject: mathematics
title: Binomial distribution
explanation: Exactly r successes in n independent Bernoulli(p) trials; mean = np, variance = npq with q = 1 − p (variance < mean always).
conditions: Fixed n, independent trials, constant success probability p; probabilities sum to 1 over r = 0…n.

subject: mathematics
title: Pythagorean identities
explanation: All from sin² + cos² = 1 by dividing through by cos² or sin²; the workhorse for simplifying expressions and solving equations.
conditions: Where the functions are defined (divide by cos² excludes θ = (2k+1)π/2, etc.).

subject: mathematics
title: Compound angle formulas
explanation: cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B — note the SIGN FLIP for cosine; tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B)/(1 ∓ tan A tan B).
conditions: Angles in radians or degrees consistently; denominators nonzero for the tangent version.

subject: mathematics
title: Double angle formulas
explanation: From the compound formulas with B = A; tan 2θ = 2tanθ/(1 − tan²θ). Substituting t = tan θ gives the Weierstrass forms sin 2θ = 2t/(1 + t²), cos 2θ = (1 − t²)/(1 + t²).
conditions: θ not an odd multiple of π/2 for the tangent form; cos 2θ has three equivalent shapes — pick the one matching the other data.

subject: mathematics
title: General solutions of trigonometric equations
explanation: tanθ = tanα gives θ = nπ + α; n ranges over all integers. These give ALL solutions, not just the principal one.
conditions: n ∈ ℤ; for sin equations α is the reference angle (arcsin value).

subject: mathematics
title: De Morgan's law
explanation: Negation swaps AND with OR; the dual form ¬(p ∨ q) ≡ ¬p ∧ ¬q. Set version: (A ∪ B)' = A' ∩ B' — used everywhere in probability.
conditions: Works for any number of propositions (generalises by induction).

subject: mathematics
title: Contrapositive
explanation: A conditional and its contrapositive always share the same truth value; the CONVERSE (q ⇒ p) and INVERSE (¬p ⇒ ¬q) form a different, equivalent pair.
conditions: Standard tool for proving statements 'indirectly': prove ¬q ⇒ ¬p instead of p ⇒ q.
